Apple is set to launch several new Home products, but according to the latest report from Bloomberg, the company is also preparing a home security and surveillance service, expected to debut in 2027.

Apple's home security and surveillance service is planned for launch in 2027 (information from Mark Gurman)

Apple is about to embark on a major overhaul of its Home products, with new versions of the Apple TV 4K, HomePod mini, and a home hub (HomePad) expected to arrive in the near term.

In a new report outlining Apple's product roadmap, Mark Gurman noted that the company's home ambitions also include a service.

When discussing the products expected to launch in 2027, Gurman wrote:

The most crucial part is the final sentence: "The lineup will be joined by an all-new home security and surveillance service."

Gurman had previously hinted at Apple's interest in entering the home security space, but now it sounds like the company is truly planning to launch an actual service.

Home security and surveillance is a massive market, with significant potential to boost Apple's services business profits.

If Apple does launch a paid home security and surveillance service, it could also be incorporated into the Apple One bundle, offering greater value and more effectively retaining subscribers.

The emergence of this new service also seems like a good sign that Apple is indeed serious about developing its smart home efforts. In other words, new products like this security sensor may be just the beginning of an expanded product line.
